selection: The first 15 repositories of the frozen list, in list order, that fit Refit's scan limits (counted independently with the same rules) and hold JavaScript or TypeScript (vilicvane/plug2proxy holds none). Chosen before any scan.
procedure: Blind: labelled from source before refit cloudflare ran on any repository in the list. In live files (paths not matching Refit's test-path rule) that import or require `cloudflare`, call `getClient()`, or name api.cloudflare.com, a grep listed every `<receiver>.<resource>.….<method>(` chain whose first segment is a top-level resource of the cloudflare SDK, and every line naming the API host; each was read in its file, along with multi-line chains. A label is one request to the Cloudflare API at the line where the call starts: an SDK method call on a client that reaches Cloudflare, a `client.get('/path')` call, or an HTTP request whose URL starts with https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4 (at the request call, else at the URL). method and path are what the request sends, with `{}` for runtime segments; null where a runtime value decides. SDK endpoints were taken from data/cloudflare-endpoints.json, which reads the SDK's source; d1 raw and query were checked to be POST.

repos.note: Wrangler's own API helpers build URLs from a configurable base, not from api.cloudflare.com in source, so they are outside the label scope; only SDK calls and requests to the literal host are labelled. A curl example in help text is not a request.

Most nodes are declarative: n8n sends requests from `requestDefaults.baseURL` and per-operation routing objects, with no call in the repository, so only the explicit httpRequestWithAuthentication calls are labelled.
Uses the 2.x client; labels give the endpoint each 2.x method requests (lib/resources in cloudflare 2.9.1).

Its Cloudflare SDK clients point at the project's own Cloudflare-compatible server (`baseURL: new URL('/client/v4', base)` with a localhost default), so none of their calls is a request to Cloudflare and none is labelled.
